findings.title: Migration crashes unless embed_category matches a category name
findings.body: The migration always runs `execute(... embed_category ...)[0]['id']`. Discourse only persists site settings that were overridden, and the join is `site_settings.value = categories.name`. On a normal install embed_category is absent or blank, the result set is empty, and `[0]` is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError. PostgreSQL rolls the transaction back, so the upgrade cannot complete and embedding cannot be moved off the old setting.

findings.title: Existing allow-list is deleted and never copied
findings.body: The copy of `embeddable_hosts` is gated on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` after a SELECT. PG::Result#cmd_tuples is 0 for SELECT (row count is `ntuples`). The INSERT loop never runs, then the migration deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings. Any site that gets past the category lookup loses its allow-list and embedding starts rejecting every referer.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are interpolated raw and not normalized
findings.body: Hosts are inserted with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` and no normalization. A quote in a host aborts the migration (and is SQL injection if that setting was ever attacker-influenced). Protocol, path, and CR from the old newline list are stored as-is. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `URI#host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`) to the stored string, so values the old setting accepted (`http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`) will not match after upgrade.

findings.title: Host allow-list lookup ignores case and port
findings.body: Lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` using `URI#host` unchanged. The column side is lowercased but the bind value is not, so a referer host `Example.com` does not match a saved `example.com` under PostgreSQL. The format validator explicitly allows `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it, but `URI#host` never includes the port, so a saved host `example.com:3000` never matches `http://example.com:3000/...`. Those referers are rejected by `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever`.

findings.title: Import passes a category id through the name option
findings.body: PostCreator is still called with `category:`, which previously received `SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category name (the migration joins that setting to `categories.name`). The new code passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, an integer. Nothing in this PR teaches PostCreator to treat that option as an id, so embedded topic creation will either raise or land in the uncategorized category instead of the host's chosen category. The new expectation in topic_embed_spec does not change PostCreator.

findings.title: Nil host crashes before validation
findings.body: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` twice with no presence check. Create/update with a missing or null `embeddable_host[host]` (and any other save of a blank host) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin API returns 500 rather than the model's format error.

findings.title: Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` load with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check. An unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404. `save_host` also assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is present, so a malformed body 500s the same way.

findings.title: Hosts are not unique, so category assignment is arbitrary
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation and the migration adds no unique index on `host`. `record_for_host` uses `.first` with no order. Two rows for the same host (easy via the admin API, or a re-run of a fixed migration) make embed imports pick an arbitrary category, so "post to category" is not stable.

findings.title: Plural id hydration throws when the ids value is null
findings.body: The new `*_ids` branch always calls `obj[k].map(...)` and only then does `hydrated || []`. A rest payload with a null or missing array for any `*_ids` key (not just embeddable hosts) throws TypeError inside `_hydrate` and fails the whole `find`/`findAll`. The `|| []` never runs for null, and the ids key is deleted only after the map.

findings.title: New embed admin API and migration are untested
findings.body: The new controller specs only assert the class subclasses AdminController. They never hit create, update, destroy, a missing id, a blank host, or an unknown category. There is also no migration spec, so the empty `embed_category` crash, the `cmd_tuples` data loss, and un-normalized host inserts are not caught. `topic_spec`'s "embeddable_host is blank" example no longer stubs a host or an embed, so it does not lock the new `expandable_first_post?` behavior either.
